questions.note: Order reads right for the scope: the hallux is longest and broad, toe 2 clearly shorter and curled at its PIP. Individual shaping is weak: toe 2 is a smooth tube widening to its tip with no waist; from below both pads are straight-sided boxes and the hallux has no base sulcus; in profile a V-notch at the IP and only about 20 mm of depth; the knuckle wrinkles are one repeated stamp.

Plates are present with thickness at the free edge, a fold rim and straight-trimmed edges; none floats, sinks or is missing. But they read as acrylic press-ons: rounded-rectangle tiles in an even gutter with proud edges and little dome, glassy plates and lips (a milk-white bead on toe 2), combed and wavy highlights, no hallux lunula, no pink-bed or onychodermal zoning.

In these frames the dorsum is nearly bare: one soft extensor ridge fades before the MTPs, no EHL cord runs onto the hallux, no slip reaches toe 2 and no dorsal vein shows; the only raised line is a scar-like arc over the first MTP. The saphenous vein is outside every view, so it is not judged.

SSS is believable: nothing glows at the thin edges and the shadow sides stay darker. The micro-relief gives it away: a dark-outlined Voronoi crackle about twice the spec's cell size on every surface reads as crazed porcelain, the plantar ridges are straight stripes through the creases, and no pores or follicles show. The declared first-pass sheen adds a glossy lip to every crease.

defects.what: The hallux nail is a press-on: a rounded-rectangle tile set in an even gutter inside one uniform raised rim, its side edges standing proud of the lateral folds and the plate nearly flat from side to side.
defects.fix: A real plate is domed (11 mm transverse radius) so its sides fall away under the lateral folds, which overlap its edges; the proximal fold is a soft cuticle roll, wider than the lateral folds, not one even rim.

defects.what: Both nails read as clear acrylic: on the hallux a glassy, even-width translucent lip, on toe 2 a milk-white bead, the highlights combed into jagged streaks, and no grime line under either free edge.
defects.fix: A real toenail is satin and semi-opaque; its trimmed free edge is a narrow, slightly irregular yellow-white band with a faint grime line beneath, and its highlight is smooth, broken only by faint ridging.

defects.what: Every skin surface carries one dark-outlined Voronoi crackle, cells about 0.4–0.8 mm, twice §3.4's 0.25–0.4 mm for toes, equally crisp on knuckle, shaft and pulp and running into the folds: crazed porcelain at native size.
defects.fix: Real toe skin shows faint, shallow furrows in a directional rhomboid net that softens on the pulp and deepens only over the joints, with pores between them.

defects.what: From below, the hallux and toe 2 pads are rounded boxes with straight, parallel sides, and the hallux pulp starts under a raised rim at its IP crease.
defects.fix: Real pulps are oval domes, widest near the tip, swelling softly out of a curved flexion crease with no rim.

defects.what: In profile the hallux's plantar outline is cut by a hard V-notch at the IP crease, the pulp hanging lower than the phalanx behind it, as if a second tube were plugged on.
defects.fix: A real hallux shows a shallow, soft dip at the plantar IP crease in an otherwise continuous outline, the pulp bulging smoothly out of it.

defects.what: The hallux is shallow for its 30 mm width: in profile about 20 mm deep at the IP and 18 mm at the nail root, against 22/19 in §3.3 and about 25 at the IP in Jeff's direction, so it reads as a flattened paddle.
defects.fix: A real big toe this broad is about 22–25 mm deep at the IP and round in section, its pad full beneath the nail.

defects.what: Under toe 2 a crisp straight step rings the toe where the smooth middle segment meets the ridged distal pad, with a thin flap sticking out past the lateral outline: a thimble glued on.
defects.fix: A real toe has a soft, slightly curved flexion crease there, with the same skin and ridge pattern running on either side of it.

defects.what: The plantar friction ridges are straight parallel stripes at one angle across the ball, both pads and the phalanges, running straight through the creases like corduroy.
defects.fix: Real pads carry whorls or loops centred on each pad; the ridges change direction between ball, phalanges and pads and break at the creases.

defects.what: Toe 2 is a smooth tube widening steadily to its tip: no PIP knuckle wider than the shaft, no waist over the middle phalanx, no separate pulp bulb.
defects.fix: Real second toes, as in the anchor feet, show a knobbly PIP, a slimmer middle phalanx and a rounded distal bulb that flares beyond it.

defects.what: The hallux IP and toe 2 PIP wrinkles are one stamp: three or four evenly spaced, parallel, glossy-lipped grooves that bump the profile like bellows (see the medial view).
defects.fix: Real knuckle skin has a loose, uneven cluster of fine wrinkles that branch, fade and vary in spacing, without proud lips.

defects.what: The 1–2 web is a flat shelf: a straight margin that drops in a lobe to meet toe 2's wall at a square corner, with a hard straight crease where it leaves the hallux.
defects.fix: A real 1–2 web is a soft U-shaped saddle sunk between the toe bases, its margin curving continuously into both toes.

defects.what: From below the hallux flows straight out of the ball with no sulcus at its base; its only crease is at the IP.
defects.fix: A real sole folds deeply where the toe meets the ball, a curved sulcus that sets the toe pad off from the forefoot.

defects.what: No lunula on the hallux and no zoning in the plate: one pink-grey tint from fold to free edge, with no pale crescent at the root, no pink bed under a clear plate and no onychodermal band.
defects.fix: A real hallux nail shows a pale lunula crescent (about 3.5 mm) at the root, a pink bed through the clear plate, and a paler band at the onychodermal line before the free edge.

defects.what: A thin, raised, glossy line arcs about 15 mm across the dorsum of the first MTP and nicks the dorsal profile in the medial view: it reads as a healed incision scar.
defects.fix: Over the first MTP real skin shows a few short, soft, uneven transverse creases, flush with the surface and no shinier than it.

defects.what: The forefoot dorsum in frame is smooth: one faint extensor ridge fades before the MTPs, no EHL cord runs onto the hallux, no slip reaches toe 2 and no dorsal vein shows.
defects.fix: The anchor feet show the EHL as a raised cord along the first ray onto the hallux, extensor slips to the lesser toes and veins as soft low relief on the dorsum.

defects.what: No hair: no tuft of dark terminal hairs on the hallux's proximal phalanx and none on toe 2, so the toes read young and scrubbed.
defects.fix: 8–12 dark hairs 5–8 mm long on the hallux's proximal phalanx and 2–4 on toe 2, lying flat toward the tip, as several anchor feet show.

defects.what: Toe 2's DIP crease is a single long, even, bright-lipped groove across the whole toe, a knife cut.
defects.fix: A real DIP shows two or three short, soft, uneven creases that fade toward the sides of the toe.

defects.what: A wavy S-shaped highlight runs down toe 2's nail beside straight vertical streaks, so the plate reads warped, like a thin plastic sheet, rather than smoothly domed.
defects.fix: A real plate is a smooth, evenly curved shell; its highlight is a clean band broken only by faint longitudinal ridging.

defects.what: From below, toe 2's free edge shows past its pulp as a clear glassy sliver with jagged corners, and the hallux's free-edge corners glint past its pulp.
defects.fix: Seen from below, a trimmed toenail hides behind the pulp or shows only as a thin, opaque, yellow-white rim with rounded corners.

defects.what: The hallux free edge's lateral corner is a squared, thick glassy slab end resting on the skin.
defects.fix: A trimmed corner is slightly rounded and dips into the lateral fold.

defects.what: A tiny bright fleck under the hallux free edge in clay suggests the plate's underside pokes through the hyponychium.
defects.fix: The plate's underside clears the hyponychium everywhere, leaving a thin shadowed gap under the free edge.

defects.what: Tiny white flecks on toe 2's dorsum and the web read as lint or dandruff, not as hair.
defects.fix: Any hair visible here on a real toe is dark brown and lies flat toward the tip.

ranked: [D1] The hallux nail, the focus of most views, is a press-on: a rounded-rectangle tile in an even gutter inside one uniform raised rim, its edges standing proud of the lateral folds and the plate nearly flat across. A real plate domes and slips under its folds.

[D2] Both nails read as clear acrylic: a glassy, even-width translucent lip on the hallux, a milk-white bead on toe 2, highlights combed into jagged streaks, no grime line. Real toenails are satin and semi-opaque, with a narrow, irregular yellow-white free edge.

[D3] Every skin surface wears one dark-outlined Voronoi crackle, cells about 0.4–0.8 mm (twice §3.4's toe cells), equally crisp on knuckle, shaft and pulp and running into the folds: crazed porcelain at native size, not the faint, directional furrows of real skin.

[D4] From below, the hallux and toe 2 pads are straight-sided rounded boxes and the hallux pulp starts under a raised rim at its IP crease; real pulps are oval domes, widest near the tip, swelling softly out of a curved crease.

[D5] In profile the hallux's plantar outline is cut by a hard V-notch at the IP crease, the pulp hanging lower than the phalanx behind it as if a second tube were plugged on; a real IP crease is a soft, shallow dip.

[D6] The hallux is broad but shallow, about 20 mm deep at the IP and 18 at the nail root in profile against 22/19 in §3.3 and about 25 in Jeff's direction, so it reads as a flattened paddle rather than a thick, round big toe.

[D7] Under toe 2 a crisp straight step rings the toe where the smooth middle segment meets the ridged pad, a thin flap sticking out past the lateral outline: a thimble glued on, where a real toe has a soft flexion crease.

[D8] The plantar friction ridges are straight parallel stripes at one angle across the ball, both pads and the phalanges, running through the creases like corduroy; real pads carry whorls or loops that follow each pad and stop at the creases.

[D9] Toe 2 is a smooth tube widening steadily to its tip: no PIP knuckle wider than the shaft, no waist over the middle phalanx, no separate pulp bulb. The anchor feet show a knobbly PIP, a slim middle phalanx and a round distal bulb.

[D10] The hallux IP and toe 2 PIP wrinkles are one stamp: three or four evenly spaced, parallel, glossy-lipped grooves that bump the profile like bellows; real knuckle skin has a loose, uneven cluster of fine, branching wrinkles.

[D11] The 1–2 web is a flat shelf: a straight margin that drops in a lobe to meet toe 2's wall at a square corner, with a hard straight crease where it leaves the hallux; a real web is a soft U-shaped saddle sunk between the toe bases.
[D12] From below the hallux flows straight out of the ball with no sulcus at its base, its only crease at the IP; a real sole folds deeply where the toe pad meets the ball.

[D13] No lunula on the hallux and no zoning in the plate: one pink-grey tint from fold to free edge, no pale crescent at the root, no pink bed under a clear plate, no onychodermal band. §1.4 asks for a visible lunula.

[D14] A thin, raised, glossy line arcs about 15 mm across the dorsum of the first MTP and nicks the dorsal profile in the medial view: a podiatrist would read a healed incision scar, not joint creases.

[D15] The forefoot dorsum in frame is smooth: one faint extensor ridge fades before the MTPs, no EHL cord runs onto the hallux, no slip reaches toe 2, no dorsal vein shows. The anchor feet carry tendon and vein relief right here.
[D16] No hair: no tuft of dark hairs on the hallux's proximal phalanx and none on toe 2; next to the anchor feet the bald toes read young.
[D17] Toe 2's DIP crease is one long, even, bright-lipped groove across the whole toe, a knife cut; a real DIP shows two or three short, soft, uneven creases.
[D18] A wavy S-shaped highlight runs down toe 2's nail beside straight streaks, so the plate reads warped like a thin plastic sheet rather than a smoothly domed shell.
[D19] From below, toe 2's free edge shows past its pulp as a clear glassy sliver with jagged corners, and the hallux's free-edge corners glint past its pulp.
[D20] At the zoom, the hallux free edge's lateral corner is a squared, thick glassy slab end resting on the skin, not a slightly rounded corner dipping into the fold.
[D21] In clay a tiny bright fleck under the hallux free edge suggests the plate's underside pokes through the hyponychium.
[D22] Tiny white flecks on toe 2's dorsum and the web read as lint, not hair.
Taken together the toes read young, scrubbed and new: no grime under the free edges, no thickening, ridging or yellowing in the hallux plate, nothing of a 40-year-old man who lives in boots.

The first-pass skin material (declared, not scored) gives the dorsum a wet, lacquered sheen; it puts a glossy lip on every crease and so makes the stamped wrinkles and the MTP line read even more as carved grooves.
